messages.author: 0cc7a87e6148a7b2
messages.subject: variance estimation
parts:
Hello,

I used a marked LGCP model, using the SPDE approach, to estimate counts in the cells of a grid. We can obtain these estimates for each c cell by: |c|*E[lambda(c)]*E[m(c)], where |c| is the area of the c cell , lambda(c) is the intensity of the point process and m(c) is the mark. Now, I’m trying to estimate the variance of these estimates, but I have some problems.. At first, I thought to use the inla.tmarginal function to transform the marginals, but in this case it envolves two distributions.. My second problem is that these marginals are calculated for mesh nodes and not for each cell. I did a projection for a grid to obtain the counts estimates for every cell. So, how would I obtain the variance of these estimates?

Any help is welcome.
Thanks in advance.

Soraia

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] variance estimation
parts:
It can be estimated considering Monte Carlo samples from the joint
posterior. Please have a look at inla.posterior.sample()

Elias

messages.author: 0cc7a87e6148a7b2
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] variance estimation
parts:
Thank you very much Elias! I think this will solve my problem!

Soraia

Hi again,


I used inla.posterior.sample, but the results for the linear predictor of the point pattern are very different than the estimates for linear predictor obtained by the model. For the marks, everything looks well..

Here is an example of the results from one sample.


#data

j.stk


#marked LGCP model

j.res


#marks index

idx.marcas<-inla.stack.index(j.stk, tag="marcas")$data

idx.marcas.v<-idx.marcas[1]:(idx.marcas[1]+nv-1)


#point pattern index

idx.pp<-inla.stack.index(j.stk, tag="pp")$data

idx.pp.v<-idx.pp[1]:(idx.pp[1]+nv-1)


samples_m = inla.posterior.sample(1,j.res)


> summary(log(j.res$summary.fitted.values[idx.pp.v,1]))

   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 

 -9.276  -6.100  -4.221  -4.115  -2.131   2.501 

> summary(samples_m[[1]]$latent[idx.pp.v,])

   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 

-18.780  -7.193  -4.463  -4.914  -2.153   2.455 


> summary(log(j.res$summary.fitted.values[idx.marcas.v,1]))

   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 

 -1.824  -1.824  -1.824  -1.824  -1.824  -1.824 

> summary(samples_m[[1]]$latent[idx.marcas.v,])

   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 

 -1.840  -1.824  -1.821  -1.821  -1.817  -1.798 


Am I doing something wrong?


Thank you.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] variance estimation
parts:
You seem to be comparing the posterior quantiles with samples. To me, the values look remarkably similar. Can you be more specific about what values you perceive to be very different, and why you would expect them to be more similar? The quantiles are very close, considering that you're comparing point estimates with samples.

Finn
